title: Monosodium Glutamate: What It Is and How Much Sodium It Really Adds

seo.title: MSG: What It Is and How Much Sodium It Has
seo.meta_description: MSG is the sodium salt of glutamic acid. By weight it contains roughly 12% sodium, compared with about 39% in sodium chloride, so gram for gram it contributes much less sodium than table salt.
seo.search_intent: Explain what MSG is, its sodium contribution, safety, and why it cannot be treated as sodium-free seasoning.

excerpt: MSG provides glutamate for savory umami taste and contains sodium, but far less sodium by weight than table salt: roughly 12% versus about 39%. It can help with flavor, but it still counts toward total dietary sodium.
content_html:
MSG tastes savory but its name makes one fact easy to miss: it still contains sodium. What changes is the concentration. Monosodium glutamate is roughly 12% sodium by weight, while sodium chloride is about 39% sodium.

MSG is a sodium salt of glutamic acid

Glutamate is an amino acid found naturally in foods such as tomatoes and aged cheeses. Commercial MSG is produced by fermentation and supplies free glutamate, which is responsible for its umami taste.

Gram for gram, it adds less sodium than salt

One gram of table salt contains about 390 mg sodium, while one gram of MSG contains about 120 mg. That does not make MSG sodium-free; it means the same weight contributes roughly one-third as much sodium.

Safety and sodium are separate questions

FDA considers added MSG generally recognized as safe. Reports of symptoms have been studied for decades, but controlled studies have not consistently reproduced reactions in people who identify themselves as sensitive under ordinary food-use conditions.

The recipe determines whether sodium actually falls

Replacing part of the salt with MSG can lower sodium if the total formulation uses less sodium overall. Simply adding MSG on top of the usual salt does not. Check the finished recipe or Nutrition Facts number rather than treating “umami” as a synonym for low sodium.

faq.question: Does MSG contain sodium?
faq.answer: Yes. It is a sodium salt and contains roughly 12% sodium by weight.

faq.question: Does MSG have less sodium than table salt?
faq.answer: Yes. Sodium chloride is about 39% sodium by weight, so MSG contributes much less sodium gram for gram.

faq.question: Is MSG considered safe by FDA?
faq.answer: Yes. FDA considers the addition of MSG to foods generally recognized as safe under intended conditions of use.
